coaching.headline: A short, brutal mugging. Every Fangtooth, Seedling, the Mini Prime and both towers were ours. They took only river buffs.
coaching.team: Clean fucking work from start to finish. The duo drew first blood, we won all three skirmishes, and our only death came in a trade with Murdock. Their mid barely registered on the damage chart, so this was not a stress test.

focus.title: Every won fight ends in a prize
focus.evidence: All three won fights were followed within 90 seconds by an Outer Tower, Fangtooth or Mini Prime, while the enemy won no fight to convert. The sequence held every time in a short game.
focus.action: After the next won fight, one player names the reachable objective or tower before anyone chases another kill. Next game, check that every won fight is followed by an objective or structure.

perPlayer.a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e: Xeebs played Feng Mao like the offlane owed him money. Top hero damage in the lobby, kills on both Steel and Scarlett, and zero deaths on a hero where he usually dies plenty. The zero is the impressive part, so treat it as the standard. Next game, when Scarlett is dead or recalling, Feng Mao shoves the offlane wave first, then joins the next Fangtooth or tower call with Earth Shatter ready for whoever is low.
perPlayer.10edbf65-457d-48d0-9151-9df5b4fcb40a: Willy's Belica was the richest player on the map and never died. Facing a Fey who barely dealt damage, he farmed well above his usual pace on the hero and killed Fey and Dekker once each. The gold outran the damage, though, with hero damage under his usual Belica rate. When the mid wave is pushed and Fey is dead or missing, Belica takes that lead to the next fight and opens with Seismic Assault for the team to follow.
perPlayer.16f28434-561f-4f23-9454-40321f4a1ef3: Goldilocks did the unglamorous shit that ends games early: the heaviest objective damage on our team by a distance, no deaths, and the kill on Scarlett in a won fight. Hero damage was well under his usual Wukong rate, and nobody cares when the pits keep falling our way. Keep that standard: whenever Steel is dead, Wukong starts the next Fangtooth.
perPlayer.7c8ab99c-31c5-4ea5-a6fa-e0d6417c3f1b: Proper support work, and it started early. Phase took first blood on Dekker, neither of our duo died in the early lane, and Mr_Meat31 was in on just under half our kills while out-healing everyone in the lobby. Next game, Phase opens fights Linked to Sparrow, who turned fights into bodies here. When Sparrow commits onto Murdock or Dekker, Phase fires Hyperflux in that window so both Phase and Sparrow get the attack speed and haste.
perPlayer.a0c393cc-1437-4bdc-8168-64676ce2166c: Five kills, and both members of their duo went down to Sparrow twice each. When Murdock is still standing in a fight, Sparrow shoots from behind Feng Mao and saves Heightened Senses to slip out once Murdock commits. Cuban Noobster was the finisher, and the only death was a straight swap with Murdock. Damage ran around half his usual Sparrow rate, which is fine when fights end this fast and a problem in a game that drags.

10.7.call: Won 2-0, Sparrow and Feng Mao credited with Steel and Scarlett. Our first Fangtooth fell just before and their first Outer Tower followed. The timing does not show who was at the pit or who hit the tower.

13.5.call: Won 2-0: Wukong took Scarlett and Sparrow took Murdock while they collected a River buff in the same window. Kill credits do not show where the fight happened or who else was nearby.

14.7.call: Won 2-1. Sparrow took Dekker and Murdock and died to Murdock in the same exchange; their second Outer Tower fell, then Fangtooth and Mini Prime. The record does not show who took each prize or whether the death was avoidable.

16f28434-561f-4f23-9454-40321f4a1ef3.matchup: Jungle opponent: Steel, a peel tank whose Spectral Schematics adds current-health damage when he immobilizes someone and whose Heavy Metal augment turns his armor into punch damage. He died twice and dealt little hero damage. The gank targets mattered more: Scarlett led their hero damage with Mutilator's max-health hits and omnivamp, Murdock roots with Static Trap, and their Fey barely registered. Wukong's credited kill was on Scarlett; the record does not show which lanes he ganked.
16f28434-561f-4f23-9454-40321f4a1ef3.build: Manta Scythe is a farming item first: extra basic-attack damage to minions and small monsters, permanent physical power from siege minions and camp leaders, and bonus damage against a target with no ally nearby. That fits a jungler whose game was clearing and objectives, and Wukong finished with the heaviest objective damage on our team. It was his only completed item, so the match tested the first purchase, not a full build. No build impact beyond that is proven here.
16f28434-561f-4f23-9454-40321f4a1ef3.eternal: Lotus hands out a random small bonus on a timer and on every takedown, so it grows with time and fights rather than giving one fixed effect. Early Bloom grants an extra level at a level threshold, which a game this short may not have reached; the record does not include levels. Immaculate reduces damage only while health stays high, which suits entering a gank or pit healthy. Masterpiece is the draft alternative to Early Bloom for kill-driven speed and damage, trading away the bonus level.
16f28434-561f-4f23-9454-40321f4a1ef3.augment: Masterful Mimicry raises Wukong's clone cap by one and generates Hair over time, so clones keep coming without needing as many hits. That supports overwhelming a target or a pit with clones. The record cannot show clone counts or uptime. Prosperous Path, kill gold in Body stance or kill healing in Spirit stance, is the alternative for a snowball game like this one; nothing here proves it would have done more.
16f28434-561f-4f23-9454-40321f4a1ef3.crest: Nex dashes and deals burst to nearby heroes, boosted by Sow, a share of recent hero damage stored for a few seconds. It rewards finishing a gank after damage has already landed, not opening one cold. A game with hero damage well under his usual rate gives Sow less to store overall, though the stored value at each activation is not recorded.
16f28434-561f-4f23-9454-40321f4a1ef3.improvement: Keep Manta Scythe as the farming opener. The common winning core continues into Infernum and Syonic Echo: Infernum ignites a target after repeated hits for max-health damage, while Syonic Echo grants attack speed after each ability cast and resets the melee basic attack. Syonic Echo suits Wukong's ability-then-basic rhythm in longer fights; Infernum is the answer if Steel becomes the body in the way. This short game tested neither.

7c8ab99c-31c5-4ea5-a6fa-e0d6417c3f1b.matchup: Duo lane: Phase with Sparrow into Dekker and Murdock. Both enemy duo players bring immobilization: Dekker's Stasis Bomb stuns and her Dynamo makes immobilized targets take extra damage briefly, while Murdock's Static Trap roots and his Long Arm of the Law can snipe from anywhere. Phase took first blood on Dekker, and neither of our duo died early. Sparrow's only death came to Murdock in a trade.
7c8ab99c-31c5-4ea5-a6fa-e0d6417c3f1b.build: Prophecy adds magical on-hit damage and attack speed to Phase's own basic attacks. It is a damage choice that pays when she can attack safely, and in a game where their duo died six times she had openings; the record does not show how many attacks landed. It was her only completed item. Nothing in this match shows Prophecy cost a fight, so no build impact is proven.
7c8ab99c-31c5-4ea5-a6fa-e0d6417c3f1b.eternal: Lotus grows through takedowns and time, and Phase was involved in just under half our kills. Flawless heals Phase and nearby allies when an ability hits an enemy hero, a natural fit for her ability-driven healing. Prima Donna raises her damage to heroes but makes her take more damage from everything. She did not die, so the downside never showed in the result; that does not prove it is safe. Immaculate is the defensive draft alternative if Dekker's stun starts landing on Phase first.
7c8ab99c-31c5-4ea5-a6fa-e0d6417c3f1b.augment: Psychic Support makes Essence Catalyst also restore the Linked ally's missing mana. It pays when the Linked carry is running dry, which the record cannot show. Kindred Surge adds movement speed and health regeneration during Hyperflux, a more direct tool if Murdock's trap or Dekker's stun starts catching the duo. With no early duo deaths here, there is no case for a forced change.
7c8ab99c-31c5-4ea5-a6fa-e0d6417c3f1b.crest: Tranquility's Grace heals Phase and nearby heroes with a short burst of damage mitigation, and Visionary grants Solstone and raises her ward cap. Phase led the lobby in healing, though Grace's share of it is not recorded. Six wards placed matched Dekker's six, and her clear was half of our team's destroyed wards while they cleared none; the extra ward capacity is there if a longer game needs more coverage.
7c8ab99c-31c5-4ea5-a6fa-e0d6417c3f1b.improvement: The common winning core runs Marshal, Enra's Blessing and Galaxy Greaves. Marshal moves Prophecy's value from Phase's own attacks onto nearby allies as attack speed and on-hit damage, which suits a team where Sparrow and Feng Mao did the killing. Enra's Blessing shields a nearby ally when they are immobilized, a direct answer to Stasis Bomb, Static Trap and Dynamo's amplification. This stomp proves neither swap necessary; choose by whether attack time or lockdown is the problem.

a0c393cc-1437-4bdc-8168-64676ce2166c.matchup: Duo lane: Sparrow with Phase into Murdock and Dekker. Murdock built Lightning Hawk himself and roots with Static Trap; Dekker stuns with Stasis Bomb and amplifies damage on immobilized targets through Dynamo. Sparrow has no dash in her kit, so that lockdown is the real threat. She killed Murdock twice and Dekker twice, and her only death was to Murdock in the same exchange where she killed him.
a0c393cc-1437-4bdc-8168-64676ce2166c.build: Lightning Hawk builds Momentum while moving or attacking, then empowers a basic attack that slows; Vanquisher adds penetration and executes a hero who drops very low. Both reward finishing targets, and Sparrow finished plenty. The common winning core is different: Storm Breaker, Sky Splitter and Spectra lean on chain lightning, current-health damage and attack-speed procs. Final inventory does not show purchase timing, and this short game does not prove either route better.
a0c393cc-1437-4bdc-8168-64676ce2166c.eternal: Weald fires true-damage projectiles when Sparrow damages a hero below a health threshold, the same finishing pattern as Vanquisher and Pacifier's low-health bonus. Forage adds gold and experience per minion or monster kill. Wind-Rider grants attack speed after a dash, a teleport or leaving stealth, so both Heightened Senses and Pacifier trigger it. That is a coherent finisher loadout. Taproot is the alternative to Wind-Rider when Sparrow needs on-hit healing to survive longer trades.
a0c393cc-1437-4bdc-8168-64676ce2166c.augment: Endless Hunt resets Sparrow's basic ability cooldowns on takedowns and grants permanent physical penetration per takedown. Six takedowns gave it plenty of triggers, although the record does not show which resets were used. In a snowball game this is the right kind of augment. Inner Fury, a wider and longer Inner Fire, is the teamfight alternative at the cost of the reset engine; nothing here argues for it.
a0c393cc-1437-4bdc-8168-64676ce2166c.crest: Pacifier dashes, empowers the next physical hit, multiplies that hit against low-health targets, and allows a recast after a quick kill. It is Sparrow's only dash, which makes it both her finishing tool and her emergency exit; spending it forward leaves Heightened Senses as the only way out. The record does not show when it was used or whether any recast happened.
a0c393cc-1437-4bdc-8168-64676ce2166c.improvement: Keep the finishing package; five kills and one death give no reason to change it. If Steel's frontline starts absorbing Sparrow's damage in a longer game, Sky Splitter's current-health damage answers that better than more execute. If the enemy duo's lockdown becomes the problem, Absolution adds tenacity, magical armor and mitigation while immobilized, sacrificing some damage. This match tested neither.

10edbf65-457d-48d0-9151-9df5b4fcb40a.matchup: Belica faced The Fey, who finished only Timewarp and dealt almost no hero damage all game. Fey's Fly Trap pull rewards clumped targets, but the mid threat never showed up on the damage chart. Across the lobby, Scarlett and Dekker did most of their damage and Steel was the frontline body. Belica killed Fey and Dekker once each. The record shows a mid opponent who did little damage, not how the lane was played.
10edbf65-457d-48d0-9151-9df5b4fcb40a.build: Combustion triggers splash burst on ability damage, with its cooldown shortening while Belica damages heroes. Wraith Leggings adds magical penetration and extra ability damage against heroes below a health threshold, a finishing layer on top of Neural Disruptor. Those are two pieces of the common winning core; final inventory does not show purchase timing. On core, nothing to teach here.
10edbf65-457d-48d0-9151-9df5b4fcb40a.eternal: Aion turns Belica's spell damage to heroes into gold, and casting stacks mana regeneration, which supports Runic Focus: that minor rewards a high current mana percentage. Bottomless Vial adds a potion charge and permanent magical power only for River Buffs Belica personally kills; our team took more river buffs than theirs, but the record does not show whose they were. Perfection is the slot-two alternative, giving ability haste while healthy instead of mana-scaled power.
10edbf65-457d-48d0-9151-9df5b4fcb40a.augment: Combat Veteran adds movement speed and passive experience over time. That fits a farm-and-rotate mid, and Belica did farm hard, though the augment cannot be credited for it. Devastating Bombs, extra Void Bomb damage on isolated targets, is the alternative when picks are the plan. Against a mid opponent who dealt this little damage, faster levels are the sensible pick to keep.
10edbf65-457d-48d0-9151-9df5b4fcb40a.crest: Soulbearer gives an active shield scaling with power and mana, plus magical lifesteal and movement speed for a few seconds. Against Dekker's stun and Murdock's long-range snipe, a shield is the right kind of insurance for an immobile mage. Belica took the least damage on our team and never died, but the record does not show whether the shield was ever used.
10edbf65-457d-48d0-9151-9df5b4fcb40a.improvement: The next item in the winning core is Noxia, which marks a hero hit by an ability and adds max-health damage when a separate ability follows. Seismic Assault into Void Bomb is the natural trigger. That is the route to turning strong farm into more damage, since hero damage ran under his usual rate on Belica. If magical burst from Dekker becomes the threat, Spellbreaker's spell shield is the defensive alternative at the cost of raw power.

a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e.matchup: Offlane opponent: Scarlett, their highest hero-damage dealer, with Mutilator adding max-health damage on basics and ability hits plus omnivamp, and Volcaic Slam adding a slowing eruption. Feng Mao killed her once and Steel once, and finished with the top hero damage in the lobby without dying. Steel's Spectral Schematics punishes anyone he immobilizes, which matters whenever Feng Mao dives past the frontline.
a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e.build: Manta Scythe gives extra basic-attack damage to minions and small monsters, permanent physical power from siege minions and camp leaders, and bonus damage against isolated targets. Omen builds Momentum while moving or attacking, then empowers a basic attack and cuts non-ultimate cooldowns, so Reaping Dash and Safeguard come back sooner. These are the first two items of the common winning core and suit Feng Mao's dash-and-execute pattern. Nothing in this short game tested an alternative.
a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e.eternal: Marrow heals off hero damage, more as health drops. Leech cuts nearby enemies' base health regeneration, and Roses adds gold per takedown and briefly strengthens Marrow after a hero kill. That rewards exactly what Feng Mao did here: stay in fights and finish them. Scarlett's Mutilator omnivamp is not base regeneration, so Leech does not touch it. Blood Bank, lifesteal built from stored hero damage, is the slot-one alternative for longer trades.
a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e.augment: Ichorous Glaive restores a slice of missing health on any unit kill and a much larger chunk on an Earth Shatter execution. With Earth Shatter's free recast after an execute, it turns a finished target into sustain for the next one. The record does not show which kills were executions. Seismic Smash, adding a knockup stun to Earth Shatter, is the engage alternative when the team lacks lockdown; Belica's knockup already covered some of that.
a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e.crest: Ortus grants movement speed and physical power on activation, and takedowns inside the window refresh it and add permanent physical power. It suits a diver who chains takedowns, and Feng Mao had three. Activation and refresh timing are not recorded, so the permanent stacks cannot be counted.
a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e.improvement: Stay on this path. The Perforator completes the common core: it ignores a share of physical armor and slows on ability damage, useful against Steel's frontline. If Dekker's magical damage starts ending dives, Dread trades some offense for magical armor and a block against magical hits. Zero deaths says that problem did not appear in this match.

synergy: Our engage/CC: Lt. Belica Neural Disruptor (silence 0.5s). Our kills come from landing burst INSIDE that CC window — whoever lands it, the rest must follow up immediately.
We have sustain (Phase) — favor the longer fight where our heals out-grind them.
Strong AoE/teamfight kit — group at choke points and fight on top of objectives.
